title: How Do You Feel Today?
summary: Learn how to talk about your feelings and emotions in English. Ask and answer simple questions about how you and other people feel.

sections.p: To say how you feel right now, use the verb 'to be' (am, is, are) with an emotion word. For example, 'I am happy' or 'I am tired'. When you want to talk about the past, use 'was' or 'were' instead. These sentences help your friends and family understand your mood every day.

ex.en: She is sad because it is raining.
ex.mean: She feels not happy because of the rain.
We felt no energy yesterday after working.

sections.p: Want to know how someone is feeling? Just ask 'How are you?' or 'How do you feel?'. To ask about another person, use 'How is he?' or 'How is she?'. People use these polite questions every day when they meet friends, family, or coworkers.

ex.mean: Tell me your feeling right now.

sections.p: There are many useful words to describe different moods. Some words are positive, like 'happy' and 'excited'. Other words show negative feelings, like 'angry' or 'sad'. You can also describe your body, like feeling 'tired' when you need sleep or 'thirsty' when you need water.

ex.en: He is angry with the noise.
ex.mean: He feels mad because of the loud sound.

ex.en: I am excited for the trip.
ex.mean: I feel very happy about going on holiday.

tip: Draw simple emoji faces in your notebook with the English words next to them. Looking at pictures helps your brain remember emotions faster.

quiz.en: I ran for one hour, so now I am ___.
She has no food and her stomach hurts. She is ___.
Yesterday, we ___ very happy at the party.
He got a new job and a big smile. He is ___.
A: How are you? B: I ___ fine, thank you.
